text:
emily: heads-up — planning Py 1.5.0 + TS 2.0.0 publish in the 18:00-20:00 PT change window. small canary then ramp.
emily: TS is moving to async-only surface; Python will deprecate the sync client (kept for two minors with warnings).
sam: ack. i'll run deploy-bot. exact commands please and dist-tag policy?
emia: (typo) meant emily: commands below.
emily: ```
Py: python -m build && twine upload dist/*  # publishes 1.5.0
TS: npm publish packages/sdk --access public && npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.0 next
Dist-tag policy: 'next' for canary, 'stable' moved after GA.
```
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary 2765439999-canary: python@1.5.0(5%), ts@2.0.0(5%). ETA +4m.
jia: quick staging smoke for TS 2.0.0 failed: ```
TypeError: client.request is not a function
  at shim (/workspace/sdk/dist/index.js:88:22)
```
jia: looks like the shim that exposes sync wrappers didn't include the new async client surface. reproducer + patch in PR.
sam: hold ts canary. starting rollback for canary-2765439999-ts only.
sam: deploy-bot, run: rollback canary-2765439999-ts && npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.9.4 next && npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk 2.0.0 || true
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started for canary-2765439999-ts. removing 2.0.0 from 'next' and restoring 1.9.4. status: in-progress.
ops: for python path we will pin a fallback on Dedicated: pin redwood@1.4.12 to fallback pool with TTL 24h. cmd: curl -X POST https://internal.ops/api/pins -d '{"package":"redwood","version":"1.4.12","pool":"fallback","ttl":"24h"}'
ops: added alert rules: token-level error rate >2% OR p50 latency +30ms => page eng-oncall. added playbook to reassign dist-tags.
nate: i'll take release notes. will mark TS delayed and note deprecation timeline for `redwood-sync`. drafting changelog PR now.
emily: rollback criteria recap:
- error rate >2% for a request type that historically <0.5%
- any production canary smoke/e2e failure
- artifact checksum/signature mismatch
- auth regressions impacting >1% of traffic
emily: monitoring hooks: ensure token-level dashboards have the above thresholds and a 30m watch window for canary. @ops @jia
sam: proceeding with Py canary at 5% now, monitor 30m then 25% if green. TS will wait for fix & re-run.
emily: action items: sam (deploy), jia (ts fix), ops (pins/alerts/playbook), nate (notes). ping #eng-oncall + #devex if rollback triggers.
emily: :white_check_mark: starting Py canary — will paste deploy-bot confirmation when it begins.
